principles.text: On an orderly pullback day, do not panic-sell winners; trail with the 9 EMA and hold for the larger move rather than selling early into weakness.
On a pullback day, hunt for the stocks showing relative strength and buy them at well-defined support levels for a tight-risk entry.
When many setups trigger the same day, either find very tight entries (3-4% stops) or cut risk per trade so even five simultaneous stop-outs only cost ~2-2.5% of the account.
If you spot many entries the same day and they all fail, the market is wrong - treat the cluster of stop-outs as an alarm bell to back off.
Real euphoria is story/fundamental-driven (AI spend, 300% growth narratives), not chart-driven; being bullish off the technicals alone is not being euphoric.
For a pullback entry, prefer the stock to bounce off support (9 EMA / prior high) immediately; do not want it to retest the support again.
When splitting entries on a larger account, use the same entry style for each tranche (e.g. two 12% halves with two stops) to keep position size and risk smaller.
